title: Impact of Indoor Smoking Ban on Respiratory Health

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID) with two-way fixed effects (municipality and period).
- Rationale: Some municipalities adopt an indoor smoking ban (treated) while others do not (controls), and we observe outcomes before and after the policy. DID differences out time-invariant municipality characteristics and common time shocks to identify the causal effect of the ban on log hospital admissions for respiratory illness.
- Estimand: Coefficient on treated × post (treat_x_post) in a TWFE regression. Because y is in logs, the coefficient approximates the percentage change in admissions.
- Key assumptions:
  - Parallel trends: In the absence of the ban, treated and control municipalities would have experienced the same trend in respiratory admissions.
  - No spillovers: The ban in treated municipalities does not affect outcomes in control municipalities.
  - No differential anticipation: Treated municipalities do not change behavior before the ban in ways different from controls.
  - Stable composition and SUTVA: No compositional changes correlated with treatment; one unit’s treatment does not alter another unit’s potential outcomes (beyond the spillover exclusion above).

## 2. R Code
```r
# Complete, self-contained R code that:
# - Reads the CSV file from the path provided
# - Runs the appropriate causal analysis
# - Prints a clear numerical result (coefficient, CAR, etc.)
# - Includes basic robustness checks

# Path to data
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s36_data.csv"

# Read data
df <- read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Ensure binaries are integer/numeric
for (v in c("treated", "post", "treat_x_post", "unit_id", "period")) {
  if (!v %in% names(df)) stop(paste("Missing column:", v))
  df[[v]] <- as.numeric(df[[v]])
}

# If interaction not provided, create it
if (!"treat_x_post" %in% names(df)) {
  df$treat_x_post <- df$treated * df$post
}

# Small utility functions
has_pkg <- function(x) requireNamespace(x, quietly = TRUE)

print_est <- function(label, est, se) {
  z <- ifelse(se > 0, est / se, NA_real_)
  pval <- ifelse(is.finite(z), 2 * pnorm(abs(z), lower.tail = FALSE), NA_real_)
  ci_l <- est - 1.96 * se
  ci_u <- est + 1.96 * se
  pct <- 100 * (exp(est) - 1)
  cat(sprintf("%s\n", label))
  cat(sprintf("  beta_hat = %.4f, SE = %.4f, 95%% CI [%.4f, %.4f], z = %.2f, p = %.4f\n", 
              est, se, ci_l, ci_u, z, pval))
  cat(sprintf("  Interpretation (%% change in admissions): %.2f%%\n\n", pct))
}

# Summary of treated/control by period
cat("Data summary:\n")
tab <- aggregate(y ~ treated + post, data = df, length)
names(tab)[3] <- "n_obs"
print(tab)

# Try to use fixest for TWFE with clustered SEs; otherwise fall back to lm + sandwich
use_fixest <- has_pkg("fixest")
use_sandwich <- has_pkg("sandwich")

# MAIN TWFE DID: y ~ treat_x_post | unit FE + period FE, cluster at unit
main_est <- function(data) {
  if (use_fixest) {
    library(fixest)
    m <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | factor(unit_id) + factor(period),
               data = data, cluster = ~ unit_id)
    est <- coef(m)["treat_x_post"]
    se <- sqrt(vcov(m)["treat_x_post","treat_x_post"])
    list(model = m, est = est, se = se)
  } else {
    # Fallback: OLS with unit and period fixed effects via dummies
    m <- lm(y ~ treat_x_post + factor(unit_id) + factor(period), data = data)
    if (use_sandwich) {
      vc <- sandwich::vcovCL(m, cluster = m$model$`factor(unit_id)`, type = "HC1")
      # Ensure the coefficient name matches
      cn <- names(coef(m))
      # Find the exact name for treat_x_post
      txp_name <- "treat_x_post"
      est <- coef(m)[txp_name]
      se <- sqrt(diag(vc))[txp_name]
    } else {
      est <- coef(m)["treat_x_post"]
      se <- sqrt(diag(vcov(m)))["treat_x_post"]
    }
    list(model = m, est = est, se = se)
  }
}

res_main <- main_est(df)
cat("\nMain TWFE DID estimate (unit and period FE, clustered by unit where available):\n")
print_est("Effect of smoking ban (treated x post) on log hospital admissions", res_main$est, res_main$se)

# By-hand DID (group-time cell means) as a cross-check
mu_T_pre  <- with(df, mean(y[treated == 1 & post == 0], na.rm = TRUE))
mu_T_post <- with(df, mean(y[treated == 1 & post == 1], na.rm = TRUE))
mu_C_pre  <- with(df, mean(y[treated == 0 & post == 0], na.rm = TRUE))
mu_C_post <- with(df, mean(y[treated == 0 & post == 1], na.rm = TRUE))
did_simple <- (mu_T_post - mu_T_pre) - (mu_C_post - mu_C_pre)
cat("By-hand DID (difference-in-means on logs):\n")
cat(sprintf("  DID = %.4f (approx %.2f%% change)\n\n", did_simple, 100 * (exp(did_simple) - 1)))

# ROBUSTNESS 1: DID without FE (pooled DID: y ~ treated + post + treated:post)
robust1 <- function(data) {
  m <- lm(y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post, data = data)
  if (use_sandwich) {
    vc <- sandwich::vcovCL(m, cluster = m$model$treated, type = "HC1") # cluster at unit_id preferred; if available:
    # Better: cluster by unit_id if present in model frame; add it explicitly to model frame:
    # Refit including unit_id only for clustering
    m <- lm(y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post, data = data)
    vc <- sandwich::vcovCL(m, cluster = data$unit_id, type = "HC1")
    est <- coef(m)["treat_x_post"]
    se <- sqrt(diag(vc))["treat_x_post"]
  } else {
    est <- coef(m)["treat_x_post"]
    se <- sqrt(diag(vcov(m)))["treat_x_post"]
  }
  list(est = est, se = se)
}
res_rb1 <- robust1(df)
cat("Robustness 1 (no FE, pooled DID):\n")
print_est("treated x post", res_rb1$est, res_rb1$se)

# ROBUSTNESS 2: Add unit-specific linear time trends
df$t_num <- as.numeric(df$period)
df$t_c <- df$t_num - mean(df$t_num)

robust2 <- function(data) {
  # Use lm with unit and period FE and unit-specific linear trends
  m <- lm(y ~ treat_x_post + factor(unit_id) + factor(period) + factor(unit_id):t_c, data = data)
  if (use_sandwich) {
    vc <- sandwich::vcovCL(m, cluster = m$model$`factor(unit_id)`, type = "HC1")
    est <- coef(m)["treat_x_post"]
    se <- sqrt(diag(vc))["treat_x_post"]
  } else {
    est <- coef(m)["treat_x_post"]
    se <- sqrt(diag(vcov(m)))["treat_x_post"]
  }
  list(est = est, se = se)
}
res_rb2 <- robust2(df)
cat("Robustness 2 (unit and period FE + unit-specific linear trends):\n")
print_est("treated x post", res_rb2$est, res_rb2$se)

# ROBUSTNESS 3: Placebo DID using only pre-ban periods with a fake cutoff
# Infer the first treated-post period as the policy start
treated_post_periods <- unique(df$period[df$treated == 1 & df$post == 1])
if (length(treated_post_periods) > 0) {
  T0 <- min(treated_post_periods)
  pre_df <- subset(df, period < T0)
  if (nrow(pre_df) > 0) {
    unique_pre <- sort(unique(pre_df$period))
    # Choose fake cutoff at median pre period
    fake_cut <- median(unique_pre)
    pre_df$fake_post <- as.numeric(pre_df$period >= fake_cut)
    pre_df$fake_treat_x_post <- pre_df$treated * pre_df$fake_post
    
    # TWFE placebo on pre-periods
    placebo_model <- lm(y ~ fake_treat_x_post + factor(unit_id) + factor(period), data = pre_df)
    if (use_sandwich) {
      vc_pl <- sandwich::vcovCL(placebo_model, cluster = placebo_model$model$`factor(unit_id)`, type = "HC1")
      est_pl <- coef(placebo_model)["fake_treat_x_post"]
      se_pl <- sqrt(diag(vc_pl))["fake_treat_x_post"]
    } else {
      est_pl <- coef(placebo_model)["fake_treat_x_post"]
      se_pl <- sqrt(diag(vcov(placebo_model)))["fake_treat_x_post"]
    }
    cat("Robustness 3 (placebo DID in pre-periods only):\n")
    print_est("fake treated x fake post (should be ~0 if no pre-trends)", est_pl, se_pl)
  } else {
    cat("Robustness 3: Not enough pre-period data to run placebo test.\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("Robustness 3: No treated post periods found; cannot define policy start for placebo test.\n")
}

# Final note: the main quantity of interest is the TWFE DID coefficient reported above.
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Negative. Indoor smoking bans reduce secondhand smoke exposure in public indoor spaces, which should lower respiratory-related hospital admissions.
- Magnitude: For log admissions, an economically plausible effect is roughly −5% to −15% (coefficient around −0.05 to −0.15). Short-run impacts may be modest but statistically detectable; longer-run effects can be larger as compliance and behavioral adjustments accumulate. The robustness checks (unit-specific trends and pre-period placebo) should not overturn the negative sign if parallel trends is approximately valid.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare changes in respiratory illness admissions over time between municipalities with and without the ban.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The indoor smoking ban is associated with an increase in hospital admissions for respiratory illnesses.
